sections.hypothesis: Graduate G2 of the exploration experiment's round 2, unchanged, beats BTC held over the unspent holdout year (2025-11 to 2026-10) on a basket of large coins it has never seen, by Kestrel's holdout rule.
sections.rationale: Who pays: crypto's risk appetite moves in regimes led by BTC; in a BTC uptrend, money flows into the coins with the strongest recent momentum (time-series and cross-sectional momentum, Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012; Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu 2022), and the regime filter steps aside when that flow reverses. Where it came from: exploration round 2 (research/exploration/log.md, not evidence): 1,760 rotation settings; the BTC 50-day filter did most of the work, and under it 90-day momentum picks beat 95-100% of random picks in-sample and 68-99% over 2022-25; a 3% margin was the one extra filter kept. On the real engine over its own coins, 2018-01 to 2025-10: Sharpe 1.51 against BTC's 0.74, +4,812%, worst drawdown -36% (the exploration screen said 1.68). Disclosures: the basket is new to the rule but not to Kestrel: its altcoins are in the locked confirmation half, read before only by round 1's two single-coin graduates (2020-25, not the holdout year); their holdout year has never been read. BTC is the regime filter and one candidate, and BTC's holdout year was already used by trend-vol-target. The holdout year of every basket coin is spent by this run.
sections.rules: Each Sunday close, while BTC closes more than 3% above its 50-day average, hold the top 1 of the basket by 90-day return (coins with a year of history), sized to min(1, 50% / its 30-day annualised volatility); otherwise cash. Basket, fixed before any look by the same volume rule: BTC plus the 3 largest confirmation-half coins: XRP, SUI, TRX. Daily bars, decided at the Sunday close, filled at Monday's open; the portfolio engine with kestrel.toml's costs (each coin's spread band), 330 USDT, warmed up from 2024-09 so the year's first Sunday already has a year of history.
sections.falsification: Run once: kestrel holdout-test UNIVERSE --strategy btc-rotation-4c --research <this note> --warmup-start 2024-09 --start 2025-11 --end 2026-10. Kestrel's holdout rule, the same as every holdout: if BTC held had a positive Sharpe over the year, the strategy's Sharpe must be at least BTC's; if not (a falling year), its return must beat BTC held at the strategy's average exposure; and its worst drawdown inside the year must be no deeper than 50%. PASS needs both. A pass leads to forward paper trading of the graduate on its own coins (a paper note then, judged at a date fixed in it), as Luke chose; a fail is recorded and the graduate stops. This is one look at one year (about 50 weekly decisions), so a pass is support, not proof.
sections.parameters: top_n 1, lookback_days 90, btc_days 50, margin_pct 3, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (G2's settings, fixed). Nothing is tuned; no other setting is run.
sections.costs: Weekly decisions, a few coins: turnover like the rule's backtests (break-even far above the cost paid). The holdout test is never a trial.
